primitives.name: Receipt Signing Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Architecture (diagram) A short description plus a diagram (link or embed) of how the governed-agent stack sits on top of {PLATFORM}: which services are used, where receipts are signed/verified, where the governance boundary sits relative to the platform's own infrastructure.
primitives.assumptions: Receipts are deterministic under identical inputs; signature integrity is preserved across platform boundaries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when signature validation fails or receipt duplication is detected.

layer2.mapping: Each receipt corresponds to a unique agent decision event; verification mirrors GSI's Bayesian update process on observed data.
layer2.telemetry: Signed receipt count per time window

primitives.name: Cost Proxy Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Metrics (refuse rate, cost saved, verify checks) Report only metrics you can trace to a real computed source: - **Usage / cost proxy** — from `usageSummary()` output (`apps/web/lib/platform/usage-meter.ts`).
primitives.assumptions: Cost scales linearly with usage units; proxy reflects actual resource consumption.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Proxy becomes unreliable during peak load or infrastructural anomalies.

layer2.mapping: Cost proxy derived from raw usage telemetry; GSE uses this to estimate operational budget constraints.

primitives.name: Refusal Rate Computation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Refuse rate** — computed from the same receipt/decision log, cited by exact source.
primitives.assumptions: All decisions are logged; refusal events are mutually exclusive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rate approaches zero if all decisions pass verification; diverges if refusal threshold is exceeded.

layer2.mapping: Computed from receipt decision logs; GSI applies statistical tests to validate consistency over time.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of refused to total decisions

reasoning_traces.think:
The governed-agent framework introduces a structured decision pipeline where each action generates a verifiable receipt. The receipt signing protocol ensures that every agent interaction is cryptographically bound to its execution context. This enables downstream metrics such as cost proxy and refusal rate to be grounded in empirical data rather than estimates. The cost proxy is derived from usage telemetry, which is aggregated into a dimensionless unit representing computational effort. Refusal rate computation relies on binary classification of decisions—either accepted or rejected—based on predefined criteria. These primitives form a dualistic system: one side governs behavior through bounded decision-making, while the other monitors outcomes via probabilistic inference. Failure modes arise when cryptographic integrity is compromised or when telemetry sources become inconsistent. The architecture enforces a clear separation between agent logic and platform infrastructure, ensuring that governance boundaries remain intact even under adversarial conditions.
